Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 310 of 1998.
With 
Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 142 of 1998 
with 
Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 254 of 1997.
lawyer:
MA Wahab ANM Gaziul Huq Md Delwar Hossain and MA Wahab Miah, Advocates -----For the Petitioners.
MA Rouf, Assistant Attorney-General with Mohammad Mushfiqur Rahman Khan, Assistant Attorney-General -----For the Respondent.
parties:
Harun and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
AK Badrul Huq, J: Criminal Miscellaneous case No.1212 of 1996, 310 of 1998 and 142 of 1998 arising out of three applications for bail of three accused petitioners under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and Criminal Revision No.254 of 1997 arising out of an application under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for setting aside the order cancelling the bail to the accused- petitioner of the said case having arisen out of a murder case which led to Session Case No. 450 of 1997 under sections 302/34/109 of the Penal Code are taken up together for hearing and the same are being disposed of by this common judgment. 

 2. Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1212 of 1996 at the instance of the accused-petitioner Bachu alias Bachu Sheikh has been directed against the judgment and order dated 23-11-95 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka rejecting the prayer for bail of the accused-petitioner raising the contention that he did not commit any offence and he had been falsely implicated in the case and on the date of occurrence he was in India. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.310 of 1998 similar plea of alibi had been pressed into service at the instance of the petitioner Harun stating that the accused- petitioner was in India at the time of alleged occurrence. Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 142 of 1998 filed by the accused-petitioner Md Badsha has been grounded on the point that he had been falsely implicated in the case and under inhuman torture, he was compelled to make a confessional statement impleading himself and other accused-persons in the commission of murder of the victim Ratan Mia. Criminal Revision No.254 of 1997 was filed by Md Hanif and the same was directed against order dated 20-3-97 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous case No.745 of 1997 rejecting his bail by the learned Sessions Judge taking the stand that the bail granted to him having not at all been misused, the cancellation of bail is absolutely illegal. 

 3. Facts leading to the four criminal matters are that, one Ratan Mia, a businessman dealing with rice, fruits and cement and also the Ijaradar of Badamtali Ghat, Dhaka was killed by pistol shot on 2-6-1994 in broad day light when the victim was coming to his residence at Rankin Street by a rickshaw. Bubli Begum, wife of the victim Ratan Mia as informant, lodged a First Information Report with Sutrapur police station alleging that her husband used to tell her that an influential quarter was very much inimical to him and Bachu, the petitioner of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.1212 of 1996, Mostafa and Harun, the accused-petitioner of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.310 of 1998 and also one Swapan might kill him. On 2-6-1994 at 9-30 AM her husband, the victim Ratan Mia went to Badamtali Ghat for his business purpose and he was returning back to his residence at Rankin Streat by a rickshaw at about 2-05 PM. When he was near to his residence an auto-taxi dashed him and he fell down from the rickshaw and the accused Bachu, Mostafa, Harun, Swapan and Ripon came out from the auto-taxi and fired on him. Accused-persons then fled away by blasting cocktails. Victim Ratan Mia was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital where doctor declared him dead. The First Information Report was registered as Sutrapur Police Station Case No. 5(6)94 out of which GR No. 1705 of 1994 under sections 109/302/34 of the Penal Code arose and out of the same Sessions Case No.450 of 1997 has arisen. 

 6. The case was sent for trial and they are now facing trial being charged under the above sections of the Penal Code. 

 9. The State contested all the matters and filed counter-affidavits in Criminal Miscellaneous case No.310 of 1998, Criminal Miscellaneous case No.142 of 1998 and also in Criminal Revision No. 254 of 1997. In the counter-affidavit filed in Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 310 of 1998, it is stated that the accused-petitioner, Harun is the ring leader of the occurrence and managed to kill the victim and left the country for a short period and came back to Bangladesh on 5th of June, 1994 only three days after the occurrence. It is further stated that on being enlarged on bail, the accused petitioner along with other co-accused-petitioners threatened the informant and her sons and the charge-sheet named witnesses not to proceed with the case and not to give evidence in support of the prosecution. It is also stated that the informant made a General Diary with the police station on 7- 2-1998. The photo copy of the said General Diary has been annexed as Annexure-D to the counter- affidavit. It is then asserted that it would not be possible on the part of informant to produce witnesses if the accused petitioners are on bail. In the counter-affidavit filed in Criminal Miscellaneous case No.142 of 1998 it has been stated that the accused-petitioner Badsha was the hired killer of co-accused Harun and he voluntarily made a confessional statement before the Metropolitan Magistrate stating all facts as to how they conspired to kill victim Ratan Mia and ultimately killed him on the date of occurrence. It is also stated that the, allegation of torture is not at all correct. It is further stated that the accused-petitioner Badsha directly participated in the killing and he fired on the victim Ratan Mia. It is further stated that on being enlarged on bail the co-accused petitioners threatened the informant and her sons and the charge-sheet named witnesses not to proceed with the case and not to give evidence in support of the prosecution. It is also stated that the informant made a General Diary with the police station on 7-2-1998. The photo copy of the said General Diary has been annexed as Annexure-D to the counter-affidavit. It is then asserted that it would not be possible on the part of the informant to produce witnesses if the accused persons are on bail. 

 10. An affidavit-in-reply had been filed on behalf of the accused-petitioner Harun in Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 310 of 1998, against the counter-affidavit filed by the State controverting the statements made in the application for bail. 

 11. Let us now consider the three petitions of the three accused-petitioners Bachu alias Bachu Sheikh, Md Harun and Md Badsha. The accused-petitioners Bachu and Md Harum are FIR named accused persons. The accused-petitioner Bachu in his applications annexed photocopy of the passport. At the time of hearing, the original passport has been produced before us. On a close scrutiny of the passport, it appears that, although, accused- petitioner Bachu is a man of Munshiganj, the pass port was issued from Barisal on 18-5-1994, visa was issued on 23-5-1994. Exit from Bangladesh was on 29-5-1994. Occurrence took place on 2-6-1994 and arrival of Bachu from India to Bangladesh was on 5-6-1994. From the original passport of the accused-petitioner Harun produced before us, it appears that the passport was issued on 28-5-1994, Visa was issued on 30-5-1994 for 10 days and his arrival from India to Bangladesh was on 5-6-1994 i.e. the day of the arrival of the accused-petitioner Bachu, In the First Information Report it is stated that the victim Ratan Mia disclosed to his wife, the informant that accused Bachu and Harun and others were in a conspiracy to kill him. The accused-petitioner Badsha in his confessional statement stated that Harun is the ring leader of the commission of murder of Ratan Mia. The evidentiary value of the confessional statement of accused-petitioner Badsha will be decided at the time of trial of the case and the evidentiary value of the same cannot be considered or gone into in considering the bail matter. It is significant to notice that immediately before the commission of the murder, both Bachu and Harun left Bangladesh for India and both of them came to Bangladesh on 5-6-1994 and the occurrence took place on 2-6-1994, The accused petitioner Badsha though not named in the First Information Report but by way of a confessional statement recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure implicated himself in the commission of murder of the victim Ratan Mia. 

 13. It is contended on behalf of the State that the accused-petitioner on being enlarged on ad-interim bail by the High Court Division threatened the informant, her son and other charge-sheet named witnesses not to proceed with the case and not to give evidence in support of the prosecution case and it will not be possible on the part of the informant to produce witnesses if the accused-petitioners are on bail. In support of the said contention a General Diary entry being numbered 375 dated 7-2-1998 has been annexed as Annexure-C and D in the counter affidavits filed in Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 310 of 1998 and 142 of 1998 respectively. On perusal of the contents of the said GD Entry it appears that the accused-petitioners threatened the informant's son Jahangir that in the event of proceeding with the case they would be removed from the world. This GD Entry cannot be overlooked in considering bail matter in an offence under sections 302/109/34 of the Penal Code. 

 14. It is also argued from the side of the accused-petitioner Badsha that he had been in custody for 3½ years. The custody of an under trial prisoner for a period of 3½ years cannot be a ground for enlarging an accused on bail specially, in a case of murder. 

 16. Adverting to the instant cases, it hardly presents features warranting grant of bail to the accused-petitioners, namely, Bachu alias Bachu Sheikh, Md Harun and Md Badsha. Since main allegation against Bachu and Harun is of conspiracy to murder the victim in the FIR supported by the confessional statement of the accused Badsha though subsequently retracted, their absence from Bangladesh on the date of occurrence has no relevance for the purpose of granting bail to them. So we are of the considered view that this is not a fit case where discretion which undoubtedly vests in the High Court Division under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure should be exercised in favour of the aforesaid three accused-petitioners. 

 17. Turning now to the case of accused-petitioner Md Hanif, it appears that Hanif is not a FIR named accused and he has been implicated in the case on the basis of confessional statement made by accused Badsha. The accused-petitioner Md Hanif has annexed his passport to show that he was not in Bangladesh at the time of occurrence and he went to United Arab Emirates in connection with his business. Passport was issued on 18-4-94. It is contended by the learned Assistant Attorney-General that on a close scrutiny of the said passport it is seen that there was no visa for going to any country of the world or to the destination and the question of Transit Visa and staying in United Arab Emirates did not arise and there is also no endorsement in the visa of date of his exit from Bangladesh at the relevant time and in view of the same his stay in United Arab Emirates becomes a doubtful matter. 

 18. It has been also canvassed from the side of the State that Abdus Sattar, the Manager of the shop of victim Ratan Mia, Ful Mia and Khorshed Ahmed in their statements recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stated that over some money transaction a serious dispute cropped up between the accused-petitioner Md Hanif and the victim Ratan Mia. It has been also contended that the accused-petitioner having been enlarged on ad-interim bail by the High Court Division along with other co-accused threatened the informant and the other charge-sheet named witnesses not to give evidence in support of the prosecution case and the informant will not be able to produce witnesses if the accused-petitioner is on bail. 

 21. Accused-petitioner Md Hanif was granted bail by the Sessions Judge on 25-2-1997 though 26-2-97 was fixed for hearing of Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 657 of 1997 for his bail filed in the court of the Sessions Judge. It appears from order dated 25-2-97 that bail was granted to Hanif considering that he was not an FIR named accused, was in United Arab Emirate on the date of occurrence and there was no other evidence except confessional statement of the co-accused and Badsha against him. The informant on the next date i.e. 26-2-1997 filed an application for cancellation of the bail granted on 25-2-97 taking the stand that the accused Hanif remained absconding even after submission of charge-sheet against him for about one year, and four of the accused persons in their statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure implicated him as the principal accused and he is a dangerous clement and if he is enlarged on bail the prosecution witnesses would not dare to give evidence in support of the prosecution case. The learned Sessions Judge fixed 20-3-1997 for hearing and also directed for the issuance of notice upon accused-petitioner. From the service return it transpires that the notice could not be served upon him as because no man named Md Hanif could be found in the address given by him i.e. the shop and the Arat and then notice had been returned unserved. The learned Sessions Judge took the view that to avoid the notice the accused petitioner had given wrong address in his application for bail presented to the court. The learned Sessions Judge also took the view that the act of the accused-petitioner amounted to disobedience the court. By order dated 20-3-97 learned Sessions Judge in reconsideration of the record and merit of the case as well as conduct of the accused-petitioner cancelled his bail. But the fact remains that the bail granted earlier to the accused-petitioner was cancelled without hearing him and he did not get any opportunity to place before the court that bail granted by the court is required to be maintained and not to be cancelled. 

 22. It is true that the High Court Division in exercising Revisional power under section 439 of the CrPC should not lightly interfere with the order of the Sessions Judge. The Revisional Jurisdiction conferred upon the High Court Division under section 439 of the Code can be exercised only in exceptional cases when the interest of justice requires interference for correction of a manifest illegality or for the prevention of gross miscarriage of justice. Since the accused petitioner Md Hanif did not get any opportunity to resist the application for cancellation of bail and also to present his case for the maintenance of the order granting bail to him though his bail was not cancelled for misusing the same, an opportunity should be afforded to him to place his case before the court. The Rule issued in Criminal Revision No. 254 of 1997 appears to have merit and the impugned order passed by the learned Sessions Judge cancelling the bail of the accused petitioner. Md Hanif requires to be set aside. The Additional Sessions Judge who is in seisin of the case will consider the matter afresh after hearing both the parties within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of the order without fail. Parties may urge the grounds urged before us for consideration of the learned Additional Sessions Judge. 

 In the result, the Rule issued in the three Criminal Miscellaneous case Nos. 310 of 1998, 1212 of 1996 and 142 of 1998 are discharged and the ad-interim bail granted to the respective petitioners is recalled and they are directed to surrender to their respective bail bond forthwith. Rule in Criminal Revision No. 254 of 1997 is made absolute. The impugned order dated 20-3-1997 passed by the learned Sessions Judge is set aside. He is directed to transfer the Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 745 of 1997 to the court of the Additional Sessions Judge before whom Session case No. 450 of 1997 is pending. Additional Sessions Judge is directed to rehear the matter in the light of the observation and direction made above within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of the order. Communicate the order to the court below at once.
